summary: Ernst Sittig was a linguist who studied at the Universities of Jena, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D. under Friedrich Bechtel). He taught at Berlin (PD 1923), the University of Königsberg (1926–1929), and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1926–1955).

Ernst Steinkellner works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner, he held posts at Vienna, the University of Pennsylvania, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and Rudolf von Roth, later serving at East India House, Tübingen, and as professor at the University of Munich from 1874.

Ernst Waldschmidt was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Kiel and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Emil Sieg, and others, he worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin between 1924 and 1934.

Ernst Wilhelm von Brücke was a scholar of linguistics and medicine. After studying at Heidelberg and Berlin (Dr.med.), he served as an assistant in Berlin, Professor of Physiology at Königsberg (1848), and Professor of Physiology at Vienna (1849–1890).

Ernst Windisch, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, completed his doctorate at Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and others. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875) before returning to Leipzig.
Ernst Zinn was a scholar in linguistics who held academic appointments at the University of Hamburg (ca. 1944–1950), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1950–1978).

Ernst Zupitza was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the Humboldt University of Berlin (ca. 1893–1896). He served as Privatdozent at the University of Greifswald from 1901 to 1917, succeeding Heinrich Zimmer.

Ernő Hetényi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied as a disciple under Anagarika Govinda and founded the Magyarországi Buddhista Misszió in 1951 and the Kőrösi Csoma Sándor Buddhológiai Intézet in 1956.

Ervin Baktay was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who studied at the Hungarian University of Fine Arts. He served as Curator of the Indian Section at the Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts (1946–1958) and lectured at SOAS in 1962.
Erwin Alexis Schwanbeck was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He completed his studies at the University of Greifswald and the University of Bonn (1840).

Erwin Panofsky was an art historian who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Freiburg under Walter Friedländer. He held positions at the University of Hamburg, New York University, Princeton University, Harvard University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Erwin Rohde worked in classical scholarship and religious studies. After studies at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the universities of Bonn and Leipzig, he held posts at Kiel, Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Heidelberg.

Erwin Rousselle worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studying at Munich, Freiburg, Berlin, and Heidelberg. He taught at Peking University, Yenching University, and the Technical University of Darmstadt, and served as director of the China-Institut Frankfurt.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen. In 1992, he served as a visiting researcher at Otani University.
Esha Meher is an Indologist and linguist who has been affiliated with Yale University as a graduate student attested in 2026.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Hanazono University and Kyoto University (Ph.D.), he taught at Carleton College and held multiple posts at Hanazono University and the Institute for Zen Studies.
Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).

Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū, served as president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997, and was a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003.

Esho Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held posts as an associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
